year.shelter: It rests in shallow lagoons near coral reefs. It shelters under ledges in seagrass beds.
year.young: Babies are born on sandy beaches and crawl to the sea. They drift in the open sea and then live near shore.

food.spring: Seagrass and seaweed. Young ones also eat jellyfish.
food.summer: Seagrass and seaweed. Young ones also eat jellyfish.
food.autumn: Seagrass and seaweed. Young ones also eat jellyfish.
food.winter: Seagrass and seaweed. Young ones also eat jellyfish.

year.notes: Green turtles live on the Great Barrier Reef all year; the water stays warm.

text.title: Green sea turtle
text.stalk_hint: A sea turtle! Get close quietly, then tap Pounce before it swims away.
text.about_looks: A big sea turtle with a smooth oval brown shell and a creamy white belly. It has four pairs of plates on its shell and one pair of scales between its eyes.
text.about_food: Seagrass and seaweed. Young ones also eat jellyfish and sponges.
text.about_home: Lives in the sea near coral reefs and seagrass beds. It rests in shallow lagoons under ledges.
text.about_winter: The water on the reef stays warm, so it swims and eats all year.
text.about_young: Babies are born on sandy beaches and crawl to the sea. They drift in the open sea and then live near shore.
text.about_fact: It grows to about 120 centimetres long. It grazes on seagrass each day in shallow water.
text.menu_sub: Glide over the reef, graze seagrass and come up to breathe.
text.menu_wild: Sharks swim on the reef, but a grown turtle's shell keeps it safe.
text.hungry: You're hungry. Look for seagrass and algae on the sandy floor.
text.no_food: Nothing to eat here. Look for seagrass meadows on the sand.
